extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR) submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Conduct single-blind reviews for DMLR submissions (including datasets and benchmarks) following the NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmark Track form; engage in author discussions, follow timelines, and provide final Accept/Reject recommendations with justification and suggested revisions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind
rubrics_metrics.description: DMLR review process is single-blind, wherein the identities of the authors of a submission are disclosed, but the reviewers' identities are kept confidential from the authors, even following the final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers remain anonymous to authors at all times; authors' identities may be known to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being assigned to a submission, you are expected to submit your initial reviews in one month. If you are unable to do so, contact your AE for a new deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DMLR prioritizes high standards for review quality over speed, but reviewers should promptly contact their Action Editor (AE) in the event of unexpected availability issues to arrange a new deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review visibility and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews will be visible to the authors and Action Editors (AEs) as they are submitted; following submission of all reviews, they will be visible to other reviewers and the authors. The authors' responses and ensuing discussions will be made publicly visible only if the paper is accepted or authors choose to make them public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that reviews may be read by authors and other reviewers; write professional, constructive reviews and maintain reviewer anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement during author-reviewer discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: During the discussion phase (after reviews are submitted), you are expected to actively engage in discussions with the authors until the issues you have raised have been sufficiently addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and participate in the discussion, request clarifications or additional experiments if needed, and ensure your concerns are resolved before final recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final recommendation and acceptance decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the discussion period, discuss with other reviewers and your AE to determine if the submission aligns with the Acceptance Criteria. There are two possible outcomes: Accept or Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommending acceptance, provide a list of revisions for the camera-ready submission. If recommending rejection, provide the authors with the grounds for this decision. Communicate confident recommendations to the AE before the review period concludes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of review format (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmark Track)
rubrics_metrics.description: DMLR follows the review format employed by the NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmark Track, which includes a set of form questions (see below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As you formulate your review, make use of the NeurIPS paper checklist and ensure that your arguments are well-justified. Follow the form questions (Summary, Strengths, etc.) when writing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not the place to critique the paper; the authors should generally agree with a well-written summary. Use this to show you understood the submission and to frame subsequent comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the submission, considering significance of the contribution, relevance to the broader research community, quality of the research, clarity of paper, and ethical and social implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission includes a dataset and/or benchmark, consider accessibility, accountability, and transparency of the artifact in your assessment of strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the limitations of this work along the same axes as above (significance, relevance, quality, clarity, ethical/social implications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive, actionable suggestions for how the authors could address limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and negative societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors adequately addressed the limitations and potential negative societal impact of their work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not, include constructive suggestions. Authors should be rewarded rather than punished for being upfront about limitations; consider whether any critical points are missing and provide them as feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims made in the submission correct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For datasets: is it constructed in a sound way? For benchmarks: are the evaluation methods and experiment design appropriate and performed correctly? Point out errors, unsupported claims, or methodological flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper well written?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the exposition, structure, figures, and writing quality allow a reader to understand the contribution and reproduce results where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clearly discussed how this work differs from previous contributions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the paper situates itself in existing literature, cites relevant works, and explains novelty or improvements over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation (datasets)
rubrics_metrics.description: For datasets, is there sufficient detail on data collection and organization, availability and maintenance, and ethical and responsible use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset submissions should include documentation and intended uses; a URL for reviewer access to the dataset; and a hosting, licensing and maintenance plan. Assess accessibility, provenance, labeling methodology, and any safeguards or consent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation (benchmarks and reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: For benchmarks, is there sufficient detail to support reproducibility?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether protocols, evaluation metrics, baseline implementations, and code/data access are described and provided so others can reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns and flagging for ethics review
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are ethical issues with this paper, please flag the paper for an ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For guidance on when to flag, consult the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. Note potential harms, privacy issues, bias, or misuse, and suggest mitigation or further review where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall score for this submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize the individual criterion assessments (correctness, significance, clarity, ethics, documentation, etc.) into a single overall recommendation/score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a confidence score for your assessment of this submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to indicate how certain you are about your evaluations (e.g., due to domain expertise, access to data, or clarity of evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: While performing duties as a reviewer (including writing reviews and participating in discussions), reviewers must abide by the DMLR code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all communications are professional, respectful, and in line with the code; acknowledge this as part of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural expectation to contact AE for availability issues
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of unexpected availability issues, promptly contact your AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is distinct from timelines: proactively notify the AE to get a new deadline or be reassigned to maintain review process integrity.
